title: Mapping and Analysis of Family Language in African Union Agreed Language and Hum
description:
1. Background
Fòs Feminista . Fòs Feminista is an International Alliance of more than 200 partners across 40 countries working on the sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice (SRHRJ) of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. In 2026, Fòs Feminista completed a three-decade mapping of how "family" has been used in United Nations agreed language - reviewing 1,441 excerpts across 180 UN documents from 1994 to 2025. That mapping found that a substantial, underused body of UN agreed language already centers individual rights, gender equality, and diverse family forms, offering feminist advocates a propositional foundation to build on rather than only a defensive posture against anti-rights mobilization around "family."
This mapping has not yet been extended to the regional level. The African Union (AU) has its own distinct body of human rights instruments, agreed language, and political dynamics relevant to family, gender equality, and SRHR - including the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), one of the most progressive regional instruments globally on women’s rights, alongside AU mechanisms with an active record on ending child marriage and other harmful practices. At the same time, the AU is not insulated from anti-rights and anti-gender actors seeking to co-opt family language in multilateral outcomes.
As such, Fòs Feminista is seeking a consultant to conduct a systematic mapping and analysis of family-related language across African Union agreed language and human rights mechanisms to produce a rigorous, regionally grounded evidence base for use in African Union-level advocacy.
2. Purpose and Objectives
The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a systematic, evidence-based mapping of how "family" is defined, referenced, and used across African Union agreed language, in order to:

• Identify where existing AU agreed language already reflects rights-based, gender-equal, and diverse understandings of family, distinguishing this from areas where family language is used restrictively or left unaddressed.

• Produce a citable evidence base to inform feminist advocacy in African Union-level negotiations.

• Identify patterns specific to the African regional context - including but not limited to child marriage, female genital mutilation and other harmful practices, inheritance and marital property rights, and care - grounded in the region’s own instruments and mechanisms.

• Analyze whether language has changed over time, assessing whether it reflects advancement, regression, or stagnation in relation to gender equality and SRHR, and identifying the instruments, sessions or political context associated with such shifts.

• Generate concrete recommendations and draft rights-based language proposals for use in AU Summit declarations, Specialized Technical Committee outcomes, and other AU negotiating processes.

3. Scope of Work
The consultant will review family-related language across the following African Union instruments and mechanisms, at minimum:

• The African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights (1981) and its jurisprudence.

• The Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (Maputo Protocol, 2003), with particular attention to its marriage, family, and inheritance provisions.

• The African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (1990).

• Decisions, declarations, and resolutions of the AU Assembly of Heads of State and Government and the Executive Council.

• Resolutions, General Comments, and Concluding Observations of the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights (ACHPR).

• General Comments and Concluding Observations of the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC).

• The Solemn Declaration on Gender Equality in Africa (2004) and subsequent AU gender policy instruments.

• The Plan of Action on the Family in Africa (2004), adopted

title: Equipment Engineer - Automation
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Missions and activities of the position

1. Project phase - owner's engineer for Maintenance

• Represent Maintenance in every phase of new equipment projects (starting with the MRS1 cross-belt sorter), from design reviews to FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up. For the sorter, whose design is already set, take over the installed system and optimise it after go-live.

• Work side by side with the OEM / integrator engineers: collect technical knowledge, challenge design choices, maintainability, access, spare-part strategy and the proposed maintenance plan before they are frozen.

• Define and verify the Maintenance acceptance criteria (documentation, training, spare parts, safety, availability targets). The Maintenance sign-off is mandatory: no handover to operations without it.

• Track and drive to closure the technical punch list and warranty issues raised during commissioning and the warranty period.

2. Technical file & spare parts

• Build and own the equipment technical file: as-built electrical and mechanical drawings, PLC and software versions, parameter backups, network architecture, safety documentation, OEM manuals.

• Create the asset hierarchy and criticality analysis in the CMMS.

• Define the critical spare-parts list (references, min/max stock, lead times) and keep it up to date.

• Reduce dependency on the OEM: identify and qualify second-source suppliers for critical parts, run compatibility tests and document equivalences.

• Propose spare-parts and supplier decisions to the Maintenance Manager; after an initial period, take these decisions autonomously within agreed limits, with the Maintenance Manager's validation.

3. Maintenance strategy & procedures

• Write and maintain preventive maintenance plans, corrective procedures and troubleshooting guides for the equipment family, based on OEM data, FMEA and field experience.

• Monitor equipment performance (availability, MTBF, MTTR, top failure modes), lead root-cause analysis on recurring or major failures and implement permanent corrective actions.

• Challenge the original design when needed and drive engineering changes: retrofits, drive and firmware updates, software or parameter optimisation, with the OEM and internal stakeholders.

4. Training & technical support

• Train the operational maintenance team (technicians and operatives) on the equipment, its software/HMI and the troubleshooting procedures; validate their autonomy level.

• Act as the level-2 / level-3 technical expert for the equipment family on site and remotely

The Merlin Pilot autonomy system powers a growing range of aircraft and mission profiles and has been proven through hundreds of autonomous flights from Merlin's global flight test facilities, including Kerikeri, New Zealand; Smithfield, Rhode Island; and soon, Bedford, Massachusetts. Headquartered in Boston, Merlin is expanding its organization to accelerate the development and deployment of its autonomy platform, helping customers solve some of aviation's most pressing challenges, from pilot shortages to improving flight safety. You are a systems engineering Technology leader who has built and run the function strategically, not just practiced it. You have partnered with business and product teams to lead the system and sub-system expectations, requirements, and verification strategy on new product development programs, and you know how to turn an ambiguous concept into a defined, testable, certifiable system. ABOUT US

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like - and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds - which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia - many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact - this is the place.

ABOUT THE ROLE AND YOU

We're hiring a Demand Generation Lead to own pipeline generation for North America. Today, demand gen at Lorikeet is spread across several people who each carry a piece of it alongside their day jobs - this role exists to change that. You'll be the first person whose sole focus is building the machine that fills our pipeline.

You'll own a North American pipeline target and work backwards from it - designing and executing the mix of events, webinars, industry programs, and campaigns that gets us there. You'll also help shape how demand gen scales as a function as we grow, defining the playbook rather than inheriting one. This is a mid-senior role for someone who's comfortable being accountable to a hard revenue-linked number with a high degree of autonomy over how they hit it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own the North American pipeline target and build the quarterly plan that gets us there

- Design and run the full demand gen program mix: field events, executive dinners, webinars, industry programs, and integrated campaigns

- Partner closely with Sales to ensure every program converts - tight handoffs, fast follow-up, and shared accountability for pipeline quality

- Build the demand gen operating infrastructure from scratch: campaign tracking, attribution, and reporting that give us a real view of the funnel

- Identify which channels and plays are worth scaling and which to kill, iterating quickly with limited resources

- Define the demand gen playbook for Lorikeet as we grow, laying the foundation for the function's future team and budget

THE RIGHT CANDIDATE

We're looking for someone who is energized by owning a number, not just running programs - someone who sees a pipeline target as a puzzle to reverse-engineer rather than a burden. The ideal candidate learned the fundamentals of demand gen inside a rigorous, well-resourced marketing org, then proved they could build the whole thing from scratch with none of that scaffolding.

You might be a fit if you:

- Have 4-7 years of demand generation experience in B2B SaaS

- Spent your foundational years at a public software company where you learned what best-in-class demand gen looks like

- Then spent 2-3 years at an early-stage startup (under ~100 people) building the demand gen function from zero - choosing channels, setting up systems, and owning outcomes without a big team or budget

- Have hands-on experience across the program mix: field events, webinars, executive dinners, and industry programs, not just digital campaigns

title: Customer Support Engineer
description:
We’re always interested in connecting with experienced Customer Support Engineers who could be a great fit for our team as Verge.io continues to grow.

As a Customer Support Engineer at Verge.io , you’ll work directly with customers to help them deploy, operate, and get the most out of VergeOS, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues and guiding implementations and migrations along the way. It's a hands-on technical role for someone who enjoys solving hard problems and working directly with people.

You’ll also help turn what you learn into better documentation and repeatable processes, using AI as a practical tool to research issues, analyze logs, and find better ways to solve recurring problems.

The Role

You’ll work directly with customers throughout their experience with VergeOS, from implementation and migration through ongoing support, optimization, and upgrades. That includes:

• Troubleshooting and resolving technical issues across the VergeOS platform

• Managing escalations and complex customer inquiries

• Guiding customers through implementations and migrations

• Helping customers optimize their environments and follow platform best practices

• Providing technical guidance for upgrades, maintenance, and other platform changes

• Partnering with Engineering to investigate and resolve complex technical issues

• Documenting technical solutions and contributing to our internal and customer-facing knowledge base

• Identifying recurring issues and turning solutions into repeatable processes

• Using AI to research issues, analyze information, improve responses, and build more efficient support and deployment workflows

• Participating in an on-call rotation as needed

Who You Are

Successful Customer Support Engineers at Verge.io are technical problem-solvers who genuinely enjoy figuring out how things work, and why they sometimes don't.

You’re comfortable digging into Linux, virtualization, networking, logs, and infrastructure configurations to get to the root of a problem. You can work independently when needed, but you also know when to pull in Engineering or other members of the team.

You’re equally comfortable working with people. You can take a complicated technical issue and explain it clearly to a customer, keep communication moving while an issue is being resolved, and build confidence even when the answer isn't immediately obvious.

You also look beyond the individual ticket. When you solve something, you think about how we can document it, automate it, or improve the process so the next customer, and the rest of the team, benefits from what you learned.

The Experience We’re Looking For

We typically look for:

• Significant experience in technical support, infrastructure engineering, systems administration, or a similarly hands-on technical role

• Strong Linux administration skills, ideally within Debian-based environments

• Hands-on experience with virtualization technologies, including KVM/QEMU or similar platforms

• A strong understanding of networking concepts and experience troubleshooting a variety of network configurations

• Experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues and working through problems methodically

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly

• Experience working directly with customers in a technical capacity

• Comfort working independently in a remote, fast-moving environment

• Practical experience using AI in your work, with examples of how it has helped you research, troubleshoot, automate, document, or work more effectively

Additional Experience That’s Valuable

• Experience in any of the following areas can be especially helpful:

• VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V, or other virtualization platforms

• AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or other cloud environments

• Scripting or automation using Python, Bash, Go, or similar languages

• REST APIs and systems integrations

• GitHub projects or code samples, particularly projects

title: Harness Engineer, Director
description:
FICO (NYSE: FICO ) is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!
The Opportunity
As a Director, AI Harness Engineering, you will lead a new internal team that lets AI coding agents do reliable work at scale. As agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness), and we're building a dedicated Harness Engineering team to own it. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will design and build harness components while leading and growing a regional team of harness engineers and setting the quality bar for AI-assisted engineering across the organization.

What You’ll Contribute

• Help design, build, and evolve the harness, the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role; you will contribute to the development, not just direct it.

• Build and maintain feedforward guides (agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods) that help agents get it right the first time and drive their adoption across teams.

• Build feedback sensors, custom linters, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers.

• Own AI governance for your region: define authority boundaries for what agents may merge unaided, establish LLM testing infrastructure, and ensure AI-generated output meets quality, safety, and compliance thresholds before release.

• Define and own cross-organizational QA and quality-gating standards, ensuring consistent, enforceable engineering practices across teams and product areas.

• Run the steering loop at scale when agents repeat a class of mistake, ensure a control is engineered so it cannot happen again - and treat repository knowledge (docs, specs, context) as the system of record, fighting drift continuously.

• Decide where each control runs in the path to production, fast checks pre-commit, moreexpensive checks post-integration, and continuous sensors that scan for drift outside the changelifecycle - keeping quality as far left as is economical.

• Establish observability into agent work and own the measures that matter - cost per merged PR,time-to-merge for agent-assisted PRs, review velocity relative to PR size, defect escape rate, andagent-PR survival rate - using them to direct where the team invests next.

• Manage, coach, and grow a geographically distributed team of harness engineers; partner withstakeholders to attract talent, set goals, and measure and reward performance.

• Work closely with other engineering leaders and product management to turn specifications and acceptance criteria into enforceable controls, and to align the harness with platform and delivery roadmaps.

• Demonstrate expertise through internal enablement, presentations, and thought leadership on agent-augmented engineering.

What We’re Seeking

• Strong software engineering background with experience in large, complex codebases, and genuine care for architecture, testing, and maintainability - you remain hands-on.

• Strong consensus building skills.

• Hands-on experience with AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, or similar) and a well-developed feel for where they succeed and fail.

• Experience building engineering tooling across a modern stack, linters and static analysis, CI/CD pipelines, containerized build/test enviro

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
Facilities Management eXpress is currently seeking a Technical Product Manager to join our team!
Do you build things instead of writing documents about them? Do repeated manual tasks make you want to open your laptop and fix them? If AI coding tools are just how you work, keep reading.
Much of FMX ’s data starts in mechanical rooms, on rooftops, and in partner spreadsheets, and collecting it is slow and expensive. You’ll start by making our Facility Condition Assessments dramatically cheaper and faster. Then you’ll bring that approach to everywhere else data enters FMX .
You’ll be the product manager for these tools and usually the one building them, going from “huh, that’s painful” to a shipped fix in days. You’ll also spend more time on site than anyone in Product, so you’ll be our scout for the problems that never become support tickets.
As the Technical Product Manager, you will:
First priority: make the FCA operation as efficient as possible

• Own the cost and cycle time of an assessment. Baseline cost per building and square foot, technician hours, days on site, report turnaround, and rework rates, then set targets with Professional Services and report on them.

• Tackle the biggest time sinks first, across scoping, on-site capture, data cleanup, report production, and capital plan population.

• Build, ship, and support the FCA tools: the capture app and field workflow, operations tracking, the mapping and floor plan pipeline, and partner data intake.

• Get on site and do the work yourself, interviewing technicians and facilities staff and routing what you learn to the right product manager.

Broader scope: data ingestion and the cost of operations

• Cut the cost of bringing customer data into FMX during onboarding, from equipment lists and floor plans to formats nobody planned for.

• Build tooling that makes data intake repeatable instead of bespoke.

• Improve data completeness, not just speed. Thin data gathered quickly is worse than good data gathered efficiently.

• Use AI where it removes real work, like reading nameplate photos and floor plans, drafting condition narratives, and catching gaps before customers do.

• Automate internal work anywhere a small tool saves real time or money.

• When an internal tool earns a place in the FMX product, make the case and hand it off well, with documentation and data model implications.

• Keep the data defensible. Speed only counts if the work holds up.

What success looks like in year one:

• You know our cost and cycle time per assessment by heart, because you built the reporting.

• Technician hours or days per assessment are measurably down, thanks to what you shipped.

• The field team wouldn’t give up your tools, and Product makes decisions based on what you bring back.

• You’ve applied the same approach to at least one other ingestion problem, likely onboarding, and cut real cost.

•
A portfolio of shipped work. This matters most. You’ve built and shipped real tools, and you can walk us through what you made, what broke, and how you fixed it.

Daily AI-assisted building. You use tools like Claude, Claude Code, or Cursor every day and have shipped working software with them.

Enough coding skill to be dangerous. You can read a stack trace, understand what an API is doing, work in git, deploy to something like Vercel, and catch the AI when it’s confidently wrong. No CS degree required.

An outcome-driven mindset. You’d rather own a number than a backlog, and watching cost or cycle time drop is what motivates you.

• Identify new business opportunities and recruitment assignments.

If you are an experienced recruiter who enjoys autonomy, thrives in an entrepreneurial environment and wants your earnings to reflect your performance, this is a unique opportunity to become part of an exciting growth journey and build something meaningful together with us.

The Senior Scrum Master / Project Manager is also the primary Agile conduit between Product Management/Product Ownership and the engineering teams, ensuring scaled Agile practices connect roadmap intent to sprint execution cleanly and predictably.

1. Agile Program Leadership & Scrum Master Coaching

• Set and enforce the standard for Agile ceremonies and structure across 12 teams; directly coach and performance-support 6-7 Scrum Masters.

• Maintain a consistent Agile operating model (definitions of ready/done, estimation, cadences, escalation paths) across all teams.

• Resolve cross-team delivery impediments and run a Scrum Master community of practice.

3. Agile Development Metrics & Quality Accountability Framework
Own, implement, and evolve a comprehensive Agile Development Metrics & Quality Accountability Framework spanning sprint execution, code review discipline, and defect accountability - from first commit through production - using Jira and GitHub as the systems of record.

• Implement and maintain core delivery metrics in Jira - velocity, sprint predictability, cycle time, lead time, throughput, WIP, scope creep, and carryover rate - at team, sprint, and rolling-quarter cadence.

title: Hydrus - Voice Contributor - English (British)
description:
About the Project 
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. We're looking for native-level speakers who can deliver natural, everyday-sounding speech - recordings that hold up whether you're reading a script or speaking spontaneously. 
Please note: the recordings you produce may be used to create synthesized, AI-generated voices for conversational AI products. Full details on how your data is collected, used, shared, and retained are set out in a Consent Form, which you'll review and sign before any paid session recording begins. 
 
What You'll Do If Selected: 
Two supervised sessions of approximately 4 hours each, guided in real time by a Session Director on a separate recording platform. 
Record scripted material in a natural, conversational tone - faithfully, without a polished, performed, or “announcer” delivery. 
Record unscripted, spontaneous speech on a given topic, matching the same warmth and pace as your scripted takes. 
Set up and manage your own recording space and equipment for session recording. 
Deliver all recordings entirely in the required language (with specific dialect), without code-switching into other languages or dialects. 
 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
Experience as a voice actor, actor, or theater performer, or a comparable performance background. 
Native or native-equivalent fluency in the required language (with specific dialect). 
Access to a quiet recording space, free of echo and background noise (acoustically treated for session recording, if selected). 
Owns or will acquire a dedicated, professional-grade microphone for the audition (e.g. RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti), upgrading to a qualifying USB condenser or XLR mic + audio interface for session recording if selected. Built-in laptop mics, AirPods, earbuds, and headsets are not accepted at any stage. 
Owns closed-back monitoring headphones (required for session recording if selected). 
Comfortable both self-directing for the audition and taking live direction from a Session Director in guided sessions. 
 
Preferred (nice to have, not required) 
Professional voice-over experience (dubbing/ADR, audiobook, podcasting) in a conversational rather than commercial/announcer register. 
Baseline audio hygiene: comfortable setting mic distance and catching noise, clipping, or distortion yourself. 
An existing home recording setup already treated for sound. 
 
Your Data & Privacy 
Before any session recording, you'll be asked to review and sign a Consent Form covering how your voice recordings are collected, used (including to train synthesized/AI voice models), shared with approved partners, retained, and how to exercise your data rights (access, correction, deletion, and more, depending on where you live). If you'd like to review these terms before applying, contact us and we'll share a copy in advance.

This is not a reporting or support role. We focus on hard skills and ownership: you will join the foundational squad and own the establishment of the data foundations for the future of the company. This squad covers the foundations everything else will stand on: authentication, onboarding, and accounts. Every existing customer will pass through the systems this team builds.

You are the direct analytical partner to the engineering squads building these core services. Your mandate is to embed within the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and ensure that every microservice, API, and frontend component is rigorously instrumented, monitored, and measured.

Engineering squads move fast, but they often lack a native event-tagging and experimentation culture. You are not a passive reporter waiting for requirements or building dashboards on request. Identity & Session Stitching: You own the logic that tracks user behavior across microservices, APIs, and third-party tools. Your primary challenge is stitching sessions as users transition from an unauthenticated state into a fully mapped, authenticated account.

Observability & User Monitoring: You manage the intersection of system performance and user friction. Using tools like AWS RUM, Datadog, New Relic, Amplitude, etc, you track client-side errors, app crashes, and latency spikes to identify exactly what is frustrating the user.

Auth & Onboarding Funnel Analysis: You monitor the critical pathways. It is your responsibility to identify native mobile/web callback configuration errors and to track linked account failures, ensuring the Auth0 migration funnel is watertight.

What you drive in partnership

QA & Sprint Ticket Auditing: You live alongside the developers, audit sprint tickets to ensure behavioral telemetry and event-tagging requirements are built into the definition of done before code ships.

title: Majors Customer Success Manager
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth - personal, professional, and financial - is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission - operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today - and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Majors Customer Success Manager, you’ll lead AI implementation, adoption and change management for Harvey’s largest customers, including leading law firms, Fortune 500 companies and asset managers. You’ll work directly with senior leaders and practicing lawyers to identify where AI can improve their work, turn those opportunities into implementation plans and lead the cross-functional effort to deliver results.

You’ll own the customer relationship end to end as the primary lead for a portfolio of strategic accounts, from initial deployment through ongoing adoption and renewal. This role combines the strategic depth of advisory work with responsibility for account health, measurable customer value and retention. You’ll drive retention by establishing measurable value, understanding customer needs and addressing barriers to continued investment, partnering with Sales throughout the customer lifecycle.

What You’ll Do

- Lead implementation and transformation programs. Assess customer goals and current workflows, identify valuable use cases and build plans with clear milestones, owners and success measures. Drive execution across practice groups, business functions and regions, adapting the plan as you learn what works.

- Drive change in how lawyers work. Partner with lawyers and customer leadership to embed Harvey into everyday practice. Develop champions, address resistance and coordinate targeted training with Legal Product Specialists. Help customers turn successful individual use cases into repeatable ways of working across teams.

- Own your customer portfolio. Set account strategy and use adoption data, stakeholder feedback and business impact to assess progress and direct the next phase of work. Address risks early and lead the response to escalations, keeping customers informed and internal teams accountable for resolution.

- Drive retention and support growth. Conduct ongoing discovery to understand customer goals, decision criteria and stakeholder sentiment. Build the case for renewal through demonstrated value, address retention risks early and equip Sales to lead renewal discussions. Identify expansion opportunities grounded in customer needs and business impact.

- Lead cross-functional delivery. Bring together Legal Engineering, technical specialists, Product and Sales around a shared customer plan. Clarify responsibilities, manage dependencies and resolve blockers. Coordinate specialist contributions and ensure their work advances the broader account strategy. Translate customer needs and delivery lessons into product feedback and repeatable playbooks.

- Advise executives and align stakeholders. Build relationships with senior partners, General Counsel and innovation, technology and operations leaders.

title: Product Support Specialist
description:
ABOUT CARTESIA

Our mission is to architect AI that learns from and interacts with the world like humans do.

We're pioneering the model architectures that will make this possible. Our founding team met as PhDs at the Stanford AI Lab, where we invented State Space Models or SSMs, a new primitive for training efficient, large-scale foundation models. Our team combines deep expertise in model innovation and systems engineering paired with a design-minded product engineering team to build and ship cutting edge models and experiences.

We're funded by leading investors at Index Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, along with Factory, Conviction, A Star, General Catalyst, SV Angel, Databricks and others. We're fortunate to have the support of many amazing advisors, and 90+ angels across many industries, including the world's foremost experts in AI.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Cartesia builds real-time voice and audio AI, and our customers put our models in front of their own users every day. As our Product Support Specialist, you’ll own the front line, the first person customers hear from when something is unclear, broken, or blocking them. You’re obsessed with the customer experience: you dig into every problem, don’t let go until the customer is unblocked, and treat each ticket as a chance to make Cartesia better. Our support function is still taking shape, so you’ll help shape the processes that define our post-sales support and set the standard for how customers experience Cartesia. This role is based in San Francisco.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Own the support queue across Slack, Pylon, WhatsApp, and email, with extra attention to priority and enterprise accounts.

- Keep response and resolution times within SLA, so customers always know where their issue stands.

- Resolve L1 and L2 issues independently across billing, documentation, configuration, APIs, and voices.

- Troubleshoot complex L3 issues, reproduce them, gather the relevant details, and escalate to On-Call with complete context.

- Partner with Engineering and Product to turn customer issues into fixes by, writing clear bug reports and creating actionable Linear tickets, and pushing them to get prioritized when customers are blocked

- Reduce repeat tickets by building internal runbooks, improving our customer-facing documentation, and sharing what you learn about troubleshooting

- Help with incident communications by coordinating customer updates, explaining impact, and keeping customers informed on progress until resolution.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- 2+ years in technical support for an API or developer product, working a live queue of customers who write code.

- Hands-on troubleshooting skills: you can read requests, responses, and logs, reproduce an issue, and tell a bug from a configuration problem.

- Clear written communication, both to customers and in bug reports, runbooks, and docs.

- Experience supporting customers in real-time channels like shared Slack channels or chat, and balancing speed with accuracy.

- A track record of working with engineers to get issues fixed, including filing well-formed tickets in a tracker like Linear.

- Comfort with ambiguity: you make good calls without a playbook, and when one is missing, you write it.

BONUS

- Experience supporting an API or developer product, where your customers write code.

- Familiarity with AI products, especially voice, speech, or audio products such as text-to-speech, speech recognition, or voice agents.

- Experience writing customer-facing updates during an incident or outage.

Note: Cartesia participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with Form I-9 information to confirm employment eligibility after hire.

MORE DETAILS

🏢 In-office policy: We’re an in-person team based out of offices in 🇺🇸 San Francisco, 🇬🇧 London and 🇮🇳 Bangalore. We love being in the office, hanging out together, and learning from each other every day.

The Veterinary Affairs Manager owns how new clinics find Pawlicy Advisor in the field: conferences, webinars, and partnerships in the veterinary space. The role reports to the Chief Medical Officer/Head of Veterinary Affairs and partners closely with Veterinary Success, Marketing and Data teams.
What You Own
Partnerships in the veterinary space

• Own maintenance of veterinary partnerships end to end: campaign execution, reporting and renewal

• Build and manage relationships with veterinary associations, industry partners and practice consultants who recommend Pawlicy Advisor to clinics

• Decide which partnerships to grow based on results

Conferences and events

• Plan and run Pawlicy Advisor 's presence at national and regional veterinary conferences and events

• Own booth strategy, staffing, lead capture and same-week handoff to the onboarding team

• Track cost and clinics onboarded per event and recommend what to keep, cut or add

• Maintain veterinary assets used in the field

Webinars and education

• Run Pawlicy Advisor ’s webinar presence within the veterinary space

• Build content that veterinary teams value and that leads to clinic signups

Market focus and measurement

• Run focused programs in priority metro markets with local events and targeted outreach

• Own the field budget and report monthly on spend, clinics onboarded and clinic quality by source

What Success Looks Like
First 90 days

• First national conferences planned and executed

• A full calendar of regional events, webinars and partnership campaigns booked for the first half of the year

• Source tracking live for every channel activation

First 12 months

• Veterinary Affairs channels are a consistent, measurable source of new clinics

• Every partnership has clear terms, owners and reported results

• A clear, data-backed recommendation on which channels to scale next year

Requirements

• 4+ years in veterinary industry roles: professional relations, field marketing, industry sales

• Previous experience owning partnerships in the veterinary space end to end, from first conversation to results and renewal

• Direct experience planning and running conference presence, with lead results you can quantify

• Existing relationships across veterinary associations, practice consultants or industry partners

• Comfort owning a budget and reporting results in numbers (cost per clinic, conversion by source)

• Strong written and verbal communication with veterinarians, practice managers and technicians

• Mandatory travel up to 30% of the time (conferences and events)

• Authorized to work in the US without sponsorship

Strongly Preferred: credentialed veterinary technician, CVPM or practice manager background; pet insurance or veterinary software experience; CRM and BI tools (Pipedrive, Tableau, Mixpanel).
How you work

• Self-starter who sets the calendar, not one who waits for it

• Data first mentality: Measures every event and partnership against what it returns
